targeted_controls.method: Loaded pinned Python module without invoking send2trash or trash_move. Pure string/path helper calls only; no files moved or removed.

findings: Container packaging delegates scanning to installed dupeGuru; these four files implement startup migration and trash behavior, not duplicate detection.

is_parent uses raw startswith of real paths: /synthetic/database/file is incorrectly considered within /synthetic/data. Pure helper control reproduces relative ../database/file metadata, contrary to the source comment.

trash_move chooses a name via exists checks, moves first then writes metadata without exclusive reservation, rollback or fsync. Concurrent calls, dangling symlink destinations and metadata-write failure are not qualified. Do not adopt this as a safe duplicate-removal transaction.
Root registry MIT metadata does not resolve the BSD notices in nested send2trash sources. No source copied into production and no upstream suite run.

Dockerfile builds dupeGuru 4.3.1 from a tag archive fetched via curl/tar without a recorded content digest, installs distribution dependencies and removes installed tests. GUI base image and icon URL are separate dependencies; this wrapper tree does not pin their complete source content. No container build performed.

CI declares five Linux architectures and build/push/manifest inspection but no scan accuracy or regression test invocation. Declared build platforms are not evidence of successful execution on each platform.

Default configuration enables IgnoreSmallFiles with threshold 10, retains hardlink matches and sets FilterHardness=95, MatchSimilar=false and MatchScaled=false. Their engine-specific semantics require underlying dupeGuru interpretation; these defaults cannot establish complete byte-exact scanning.
Root MIT license fully read; nested send2trash BSD notices remain separate licensing context. Default Qt state points file browser at /storage. No production adoption.
